violations.text: Establishment's Rhode Island Manager Certified In Food Safety license is expired. FMC to re-instate or PIC to apply. Application provided during time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 09/16/2026

Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. PIC informed and guidance document provided. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/19/2026

Raw animal foods were not stored properly to prevent cross-contamination (raw shelled eggs over clam bellies). Except when combined as ingredients, different types of raw animal foods must be separated from each other during storage by using separate equipment or arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. Items were replaced during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/19/2026

-Garlic butter was observed held at 64 degrees Fahrenheit at room temperature. Butter was buried with ice to chill. -Egg wash was observed 44-55 degrees Fahrenheit. Egg wash was voluntarily disposed of due to quality per PIC. -Cheese was observed at 48 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 door reach-in in storage room. Cheese was recently delivered and placed into freezer to blast chill; over stock of bread in plastic bags affecting air flow; items were replaced and ambient of unit went down to 40 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/19/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Soup was observed at 147 degrees Fahrenheit in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Soup was divided into more containers and immediately placed on ice baths to begin cooling process. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/19/2026

Flies were observed in establishment during time of inspection Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. Screen doors were closed during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/19/2026

The floor and wall junctures in the hallway leading to the prep room do not have coving. The floor and wall junctures must be coved and closed to no larger than 1/32nd of an inch. New Violation. Correct By: 09/19/2026

Unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment, clutter or items were observed in the storage room. Establishments shall be kept free of unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment and litter to prevent harborage conditions. New Violation. Correct By: 09/02/2026

The ceilings and walls throughout the kitchen cookline area have an accumulation of grease and soil residue. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 09/19/2026

The following areas are in poor repair: 1. painted floors at bar area 2. prep room painted concrete floors 3. floor tiles near cookline 4. wall leading to storage room The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 11/19/2026

Egg wash was observed held at 45 degrees Fahrenheit. Foods were assessed and additional ice was added during time of inspection. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/15/2025
Gaskets on the 1 door reach in and 3 door lowboy were observed in poor repair. Equipment to be in good repair and proper adjustment. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2025
The floors in the kitchen and in the back prep room were observed in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 05/15/2026
